thread.title: UPRO Has Gotten Its 20% Correction, Time For A Reversal? - ProShares UltraPro S&P 500 ETF (NYSEARCA:UPRO)

author: Todd Akin
title: UPRO Has Gotten Its 20% Correction, Time For A Reversal? - ProShares UltraPro S&P 500 ETF (NYSEARCA:UPRO)
text:
ProShares UltraPro S&P 500 ETF ( UPRO ) reached bear market territory recently since it has now pulled back over 20% from its former highs set in 2018. Of course, I am referring to the parent index of UPRO, or the S&P 500 ( SPY ), when discussing the amount of a correction that the market has had. Other key indexes, such as the Russell 2000 ( IWM ) and Nasdaq Select 100 ( XLK ), have also corrected at least 20% from their highs. For those who are new to leveraged ETFs, UPRO has an expense ratio of .92, which is relatively low among leveraged ETFs. Here is more on what the fund tries to accomplish :
The investment seeks daily investment results- before fees and expenses- that correspond to three times (3x) the daily performance of the S&P 500-® Index. The fund invests in financial instruments that ProShare Advisors believes- in combination- should produce daily returns consistent with the fund's investment objective. The index is a measure of large-cap U.S. stock market performance. The fund is non-diversified.
The pullback in the overall market has been due to fears of rising rates that will eventually slow global growth. These series of events, therefore, are predicted to signal a "top" in U.S. earnings growth, and the end of the second longest bull market in history.
These fears are warranted, as interest rates are rising, indeed, and GDP is expected to slow from around 4% to 2%. Earnings growth is expected to slow, too, from around 10% to 7%. However, these are not recessionary numbers by any means, which is what the market has priced equities for with this current 20% plus haircut. Also, interest rates remain low on a historical basis.
As a result, shares of UPRO are looking attractive enough in the low $30s to attempt doing another round of buying at since shares have almost 100% upside ahead of them now if they can return to former highs of around $59.
On the other hand, if the market moves lower from here, money management will continue to be key. Let's discuss some of these strategies, and when we will apply them, further below.
The Market Got Its 20% Correction, Time To Add? I have been emphasizing how important money management is in a down market. Nibbling on positions at the 10% correction mark made sense in retrospect, even though investors like myself ended up paying pretty dearly. At least it was only a nibble, and the long-term price paid was still a value.
But, adding more aggressively near the 20% correction mark, in my opinion, offers a better risk/reward setup for investors looking to go long the market. Be careful here, though, as we are not out of the woods yet.
Stocks like Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Boeing ( BA ) are still up over 100% from their breakout levels in 2016 and could drag UPRO to the mid $20s. So, to determine the best entry points for UPRO, let's examine the one-year chart below.
UPRO Technicals Seem Bullish As investors can see below, UPRO is trying to find a bottom on the 200-day moving average.
Source: E*TRADE
After shares briefly broke the 200-day moving average, UPRO rallied back with a bullish engulfing pattern the very next day. Structural support also came into play at the 2017 breakout level, which corresponds with where the bounce on the 200-day moving average just took place. The RSI being oversold on a one-year timeframe helped add strength to the rally in UPRO, as well.
Of course, UPRO is following the SPY. So, when the ETF bounces off of the 200-day moving average, one may need to look to the actual SPY to see what support area is actually in play.
UPRO Parent Index - S&P 500 Single Leveraged ETF When investors examine a chart of the S&P 500, they see a more encouraging picture. While shares of UPRO and SPY did break the 200-day moving average on a one-year timeframe, a max timeframe below shows that the SPY found support on the 50-day moving average.
Source: E*TRADE
The 50-day moving average, on a max timeframe, is a key support line for the SPY, and a hammer is developing around the $250 area most likely because of the support line (or a V-shaped bottom using a line chart).
I should also point out that the RSI on SPY is nearly oversold at 40 on a max timeframe as well, which is extremely bullish to a chart technician. When stars can align on multiple timeframes like we are seeing in UPRO and SPY (on a one-year chart and max timeframe chart), the odds increase sharply for a rally. Consequently, this is where investors should begin doing another round of buying in for their portfolios, especially if they are looking to lock in cheap shares in a quality index for retirement.
However, if the 50-day moving average does indeed fail on SPY, due perhaps to Apple ( AAPL ) cutting guidance, for example, then the next support area would be the 200-day moving average (again, on a max timeframe). This is where support held for nearly a three-year period (2014-2016), so I expect this area to usher in institutional buying.
As a result, I will do my next round of buying at these levels in UPRO (mid $20s) if we are lucky enough to get there. I may even sell puts at the SPY $200 level (UPRO mid $20s), as premiums would be too attractive to ignore for a leveraged ETF like UPRO if a fall of that magnitude were to occur in SPY.
Risks To Strategy If I choose to sell puts and end up getting assigned to shares of UPRO around $25 (SPY $200), I don't mind getting put to those shares since, long term, prices are a steal. After all, the S&P 500 is trading at only 14x to 15x earnings at current levels, which is below the historical 16x earnings.
So, a fall to the $200 on SPY, or $25 for UPRO, would allow investors to buy at a key long-term support level with an even cheaper P/E multiple than the market is currently trading at.
However, sometimes the market anticipates these support areas and buys prematurely to prevent fear of missing out, and this is why higher highs and higher lows are formed in uptrends. For this reason, I will always be slightly anticipatory of these support levels and will buy a few points ahead of support. I don't mind taking short-term pain in order to lock in attractive prices for a long-term retirement strategy.
Conclusion UPRO is trying to reverse off of its 200-day moving average but severe technical damage has been inflicted on UPRO's parent ETF in the SPY, as it has clearly broken its 200-day moving average. Normally, investors would want to stay away from a move down like this and run for the hills.
However, the SPY has had its 20% correction, is on attractive support on a max timeframe chart, and trades below its historical price to earnings multiple. GDP is also expected to be around 2% next year, and the number of rate hikes is expected to diminish to less than two. Markets need a wall of worry to climb, and I'll take this bit of bad news with China over a sub-prime mortgage crisis any day. China is always a scapegoat, and yet the market usually seems to shake off these worries and move higher.
As a result, investors need to be prudent, ignore the noise, and pay attention to what matters: the fundamentals and technical buying points on the charts. By all accounts, those indicators are looking constructive. At any rate, preserving cash for when buy targets are reached will be the best way to manage risk in a volatile market, while maximizing reward for the long term.
